source_text: Si res quae decenter ordinata est, ad Deum pertinet, et res quae ad Deum pertinet, bona est; bonum est itaque subditum esse diabolo, quoniam institutus a Deo per hoc ordo servatur. Sequiturque ut malum sit rebellare diabolo, quoniam per resultationem institutus a Deo ordo turbatur
pass_a_gloss: If res which decenter ordinata is, to God pertinet, and res which to God pertinet, goods is; good is and-so subditum to-be to-the-devil, quoniam institutus from to-God through this ordo servatur. Sequiturque so-that/as evil may-be rebellare to-the-devil, quoniam through resultationem institutus from to-God ordo turbatur.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: If something properly ordered belongs to God, and something belonging to God is good, then being subject to the devil is good, since the order established by God is preserved in this way. It follows that rebelling against the devil is evil, since resistance disturbs the order established by God.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
